newsitem.title: USA: NYC sees next bond sale in May with $300 mln issue.
newsitem.headline: NYC sees next bond sale in May with $300 mln issue.

text.p: A New York City official said Wednesday the city, which earlier sold $815 million of bonds, next planned to sell general obligation bonds in May with an approximately $300 million offering.
"(The city) will not be back until May, with around $300 million of new-money, tax-exempt, general obligation bonds," the city official said. He declined to be named.
He added that the city, which for the second time sold taxable debt to European investors, did not now plan any additional overseas offerings in the 1997 fiscal year, which ends on June 30.

The $300 million offering of floating rate debt was priced at 28 basis points over LIBOR, which was at the low-end of projections that ranged from 30 to 35 basis points on Tuesday evening, and 28 to 32 basis points on Wednesday morning.

The city estimated that selling the debt overseas, with its first floating rate issue, saved 60 basis points as the issues did not have to be backed by a letter of credit, unlike the bonds sold in the U.S. that were refunded.

On a present value basis, New York City, one of the very few municipal issuers that sells enough taxable debt and whose name is known well enough to tap overseas markets, saved about six percent of the refunded bonds in the domestic and foreign debt sales, the city official said.

He added that the city was able to increase the size of its tax-exempt sale to U.S. investors to about $808 million from the $550 million level originally planned because the issue was oversubscribed. The city got around $237 million of retail orders and $550 of institutional priority orders, though no maturities were closed.

The tax-exempt issues initially were priced at 6.32 percent for the top tax-exempt yield in 2025, according to the senior manager of the syndicate, Goldman Sachs. And only the 2004 issue was later repriced, when its yield was cut by five basis points to 5.50 percent, the city official said.
